subject: Future Tech
title: Consent and Future Generations
description: A fast breakdown of Consent and Future Generations for builders.

hook.text: If we edit an embryo's genes, that person never consented. Neither do their children, grandchildren, or any descendants.

buildup.text: Medical ethics require informed consent. An embryo cannot give it, and future generations have no voice at all.

discovery.text: Some ethicists argue that preventing a deadly disease is implied consent.

twist.text: But what counts as a disease? Deafness, dwarfism, and autism are conditions that many affected people don't want 'fixed.

climax.text: Drawing the line between therapy and enhancement requires societal input, not just scientists making decisions alone.

punchline.text: Editing the unborn is a promise no one asked for.

quiz.question: Why is consent a unique challenge in germline gene editing?
options: Embryos and future generations cannot consent
